findings.title: Renderer must switch on five outcome kinds, but four of them have no specified or tested output
findings.description: Task 8 requires an exhaustive `switch` on `outcome.kind` with a `never` check, and the design's `AdoptionOutcome` union has five kinds (`adoption-in-progress`, `adoption-closed`, `already-planned`, `brownfield`, `greenfield`). Task 8's bullet list only says the outcome bullet carries "outcome and reason" and only describes source volume "when the outcome carries it"; Task 8T then enumerates brownfield, adoption-in-progress, `NOT_EVALUATED`, the notice, "none found" and squadron — no case for `adoption-closed`, `already-planned` or `greenfield`. The design's Technical Requirement asks for `renderAdoptionFacts` over "every outcome," and since those three kinds are unreachable through the resolver (Task 9 step 3 selects only brownfield/adoption-in-progress/explicit), a junior AI will either invent bullet text with no test or add a silent fallthrough — which AGENTS.md forbids. Fix by naming the text for the three unreachable kinds, or by having Task 8 throw an explicit `AdoptionError`/`Error` for them and adding those cases to 8T.

findings.title: Squadron bullet test is circular and never pins the required D8 text
findings.description: Task 8T's only assertion about the squadron bullet is "the squadron bullet equals `renderSquadronFact()`" — a self-referential check that passes whatever string the function returns. D8 specifies the sentence verbatim ("Squadron: unavailable. This cf version does not run squadron's capability probe, so no probe output is present.") and it is the load-bearing statement the guide prompt keys its CF-only path on (the one live check is Task 15's step-2 walkthrough). Assert the literal string in 8T so 262's isolated-function replacement is protected by a test, not only by a manual run.

findings.title: Task 12 is the largest single task in the breakdown and puts 13 fixtures in one test file
findings.description: Task 12 (effort 3) enumerates fixtures 1–13 including a shallow `git clone --depth 1 file://` of another fixture and a monorepo with moved source, into either `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts` or `pipeline-integration.test.ts` — the latter already exists and both risk the ~300-line source convention. Splitting into two tasks with their own commits (1–7 detection outcomes; 8–13 state, phase, explicit-instruction, read-only and missing-profile) would give a junior AI two verifiable checkpoints. The fixture list itself is not scope creep: each entry maps to the design's Technical Requirements.

findings.title: Context Summary's claim that 260's detection tests already use `it.skipIf` is not visible in `tests/detection`
findings.description: The skip instruction in 3T (`chmod 000`/`EACCES`) and 9T (`chmod 444`) is correct and necessary — I confirmed `pathPresent` rethrows non-ENOENT errors, so those tests genuinely cannot pass as root — but grepping `packages/core/tests/detection` for `skipIf`, `chmod`, `platform` or `EACCES` returns nothing, so the phrase "as the 260 detection tests do" points at no precedent I could find. Drop the appeal to precedent or name where it actually lives, so the junior AI does not go hunting.

findings.title: `context_build` returning the `AdoptionError` is covered only by existing generic handling plus the walkthrough
findings.description: The functional requirement names both surfaces: "cf build exits non-zero …; `context_build` returns it as an error." Task 10T asserts rejection at the integrator, fixture 12 asserts it at the pipeline, and Task 15 step 4 checks the CLI exit live; on the MCP side the requirement falls out of `generateContext` throwing into `registerContextTools`' existing catch → `errorResult` (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:92-93,210-215`). Task 11 adds only the `persist`/`read-only` assertions to `contextTools.test.ts`. If that file has no existing case where the mocked `generateContextFromProject` rejects, one line asserting `isError` for an `AdoptionError` would close the surface-level requirement explicitly; I did not verify whether such a case already exists there.
